findings.issue: Враг-attestation is NOT bound to THIS thaw's content — it is a generic, forgeable audit label. Two concrete gaps, both verified by direct probe: (1) STALE corpus_ref: `git cat-file -e <sha>:corpus.jsonl` only tests REACHABILITY of any sha where corpus.jsonl ever existed. A line citing the oldest corpus commit (78b06c3) PASSES. The check never requires corpus_ref to equal the CURRENT corpus blob, nor to be an ancestor of HEAD. This directly contradicts ADR §2-Q2 point 2 ('детерминированный якорь … на момент аттестации … не подделать'). (2) UNBOUND families: any family present in the T-0152 catalog passes, regardless of whether it covers the file being thawed. A thaw of object-handle-isolation.sh citing TENANT-ISO (unrelated surface) PASSES. The delegate never cross-checks families against the thawed file's enforcement surface. Net: the auto_additive jsonl line — which is the founder's post-hoc audit artifact under NF-5 and the entire trust basis of D-060's 'founder reviews retroactively' guarantee — can assert a coverage claim (which families, which corpus) that is false for the actual thawed surface. On the SECURITY META-GATE this audit integrity is load-bearing, not cosmetic. Live exploitation is mitigated (the enemy test must be green on the same commit per D-056), so this is not a full bypass — but it is a real, precise integrity defect in the gate's own attestation contract and an ADR deviation.
findings.suggestion: Tighten attestation_valid: (a) require corpus_ref to be an ANCESTOR of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <corpus_ref> HEAD`) AND to resolve to the SAME corpus.jsonl blob currently on HEAD (`git rev-parse <corpus_ref>:CORPUS_REL` == `git rev-parse HEAD:CORPUS_REL`), so a stale/foreign anchor is rejected; (b) bind families to the thawed surface — require that each declared family's catalog entry ('Enforced by.' line) references the file being thawed, OR at minimum that the delegate is passed the thawed file and rejects an attestation whose families' enforcement set is disjoint from it. If the architect's position is that the label is intentionally non-binding (security rests solely on the live enemy test), then the ADR §2-Q2 wording ('детерминированный якорь', 'не подделать без зелёного Врага') must be corrected to say so explicitly and the audit-record claim downgraded — silent divergence between stated and actual binding on the security meta-gate is itself the defect.

findings.issue: The handoff and ADR repeatedly state the founder path FF-FCI12 is 'byte-equivalent'. The SANCTION line is byte-identical, but the AUDIT line gained ` class=founder` (additive token before branch=). So the OUTPUT is not byte-identical. Behaviorally it IS equivalent — same grant, same exit code, ERRORS unchanged — and the added token is what AC-7 requires (machine-distinguishable classes). The claim is just imprecise.
findings.suggestion: Reword the handoff/ADR to 'founder path is behaviorally equivalent; AUDIT line additively gains class=founder per AC-7' instead of 'byte-equivalent'. No code change needed.

Plus two nits: 'byte-equivalent' founder-path claim is overstated (additive class=founder audit token; behaviorally equivalent), and missing self-test coverage for comment-deletion / stale-corpus / absent-at-BASE paths.
